en: to tilt; to slant; to move slantwise repeatedly

examples.ko: 그는 고개를 갸웃거리며 문제를 다시 읽었어요.
examples.en: He tilted his head and read the problem again.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 들었는지 사람들이 지도를 보고 고개를 갸웃거려요.
examples.en: People look at the map and tilt their heads, wondering if they took a wrong turn.
The child tilted her head for a while and then asked a question.

examples.ko: 제 말에 친구가 고개를 갸웃거리는 거예요.
examples.en: My friend was tilting his head at what I said.
Everyone tilted their heads at the strange sound.
You know the answer, so why do you keep tilting your head?

explain: '고개를 갸웃거리다'는 모르겠거나 이상하다고 느낄 때 자연스럽게 하는 몸짓이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 강아지나 고양이에게도 써요. '갸우뚱거리다'와 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '고개를 갸웃거리다' is the natural gesture of tilting your head when unsure or finding something strange. It is used for people and also for dogs and cats. It can almost always be swapped with '갸우뚱거리다'.

en: to give a look; to pay attention

examples.ko: 사람들이 그 낡은 가방은 거들떠보지도 않아요.
examples.en: People don't even glance at that worn-out bag.

examples.ko: 바쁜지 제 인사는 거들떠보지 않고 지나갔어요.
examples.en: He must have been busy; he walked past without even looking at my greeting.

examples.ko: 아무도 거들떠보지 않던 책이 갑자기 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: A book nobody had paid attention to suddenly became popular.
Nobody gave me a second look, so I felt lonely.

examples.ko: 시장에서 이 옷을 거들떠본 사람은 한 명도 없었어요.
examples.en: Not a single person at the market even looked at these clothes.
Who would even bother to look at something like this?

explain: 거의 '거들떠보지도 않다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써서 '관심을 두지 않는다'는 뜻으로 나와요. 긍정문으로 쓰면 어색해서 '쳐다보다'나 '관심을 갖다'를 써요. 무시당하거나 인기가 없는 상황에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It almost always appears with a negative, like '거들떠보지도 않다', meaning 'to show no interest'. In a positive sentence it sounds odd, so people use '쳐다보다' or '관심을 갖다' instead. You often hear it in situations of being ignored or unpopular.

examples.en: I polished my shoes and went to the interview.
I bought wax to polish my car on the weekend.
My father polishes his shoes every day.

examples.ko: 마루를 광낼 때는 마른 걸레를 쓰세요.
examples.en: Use a dry cloth when you polish the floor.
I have a date today, so I shined my shoes.

examples.ko: 바빠서 구두를 광내지 않고 그냥 나왔어요.
examples.en: I was busy, so I left without polishing my shoes.

explain: '광나다'는 저절로 반짝이는 상태이고, '광내다'는 사람이 닦아서 일부러 반짝이게 하는 거예요. 둘은 짝처럼 같이 알아 두면 좋아요. 구두, 마루, 차처럼 닦을 수 있는 물건에 써요.
explain_en: '광나다' describes something shining by itself, while '광내다' means a person deliberately makes it shine by rubbing. It helps to learn them as a pair. It is used for things you can wipe or buff, like shoes, floors and cars.

examples.en: Stop the grumbling and do as you're told.
Don't go on with your useless talk.
There was so much needless talk that the meeting got long.
Stop the chatter and let's start with the work.

examples.ko: 불만이 있어도 군소리 한마디 안 했어요.
examples.en: Even though he was unhappy, he didn't say a single complaint.
The child took the medicine without any fuss.

explain: 쓸데없는 말이나 불평을 가리키고, '군소리하지 마', '군소리 없이'처럼 자주 써요. '군말'과 거의 비슷한데, 말투가 더 가볍고 구어에서 자주 들려요. 부탁이나 지시를 하면서 조금 짜증 난 느낌으로 쓸 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to needless talk or complaints and is often used as '군소리하지 마' or '군소리 없이'. It is nearly the same as '군말' but sounds lighter and shows up more in spoken language. It is often used with a slightly annoyed tone when giving a request or order.

examples.en: My younger sibling listens to music while wiggling their toes.

examples.ko: 그는 손가락을 까딱거려서 저를 오라고 했어요.
examples.en: He wiggled his finger to tell me to come over.
Instead of answering, he nodded slightly.
The kids sit on the chairs and swing their legs a little.
Please don't jiggle your leg during class.
The puppy looks at me, wagging its tail a little.

explain: '까닥거리다'와 거의 같지만, 손가락·발끝·꼬리처럼 작은 부분을 가볍게 움직일 때도 잘 어울려요. 수업이나 회의에서 다리를 떠는 습관을 말할 때처럼 일상에서도 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '까닥거리다', but it also fits well when you move a small part such as a finger, toe or tail. It is used in daily life too, for example about a habit of jiggling your leg in class or meetings.

examples.en: Don't dawdle every morning; get ready quickly.
The bus is coming, so why are you dawdling like this?

examples.ko: 친구랑 수다 떨며 꾸물대다가 기차를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: I lingered chatting with a friend and missed the train.
I saw a bug wriggling on the floor.
A caterpillar is wriggling on the leaf.

examples.ko: 숙제 안 하고 꾸물대면 밤새워야 해요.
examples.en: If you dawdle and don't do your homework, you'll have to stay up all night.

explain: 사람에게 쓰면 '빨리 안 하고 시간을 끈다'는 불만이 담겨서 '꾸물대지 마'처럼 재촉하는 말로 자주 나와요. 벌레에게는 그런 불만 없이 모습만 말해요. 손가락이나 발가락을 조금씩 움직이는 건 '꼼지락대다'라서 달라요.
explain_en: With people it carries a complaint that they are wasting time, so it often shows up as a hurry-up phrase like '꾸물대지 마'. With bugs it just describes the movement, with no complaint. Moving fingers or toes a little at a time is '꼼지락대다', which is different.

examples.en: I heard my friends snickering behind me.
I chuckled to myself while reading a comic book.
What's so funny that you're snickering?
The kids were giggling secretly and got caught by the teacher.
My younger sibling is giggling while watching a video.

examples.ko: 낄낄대지 말고 무슨 일인지 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Stop snickering and tell me what's going on.

explain: 입을 다문 채 억누르듯 짧게 웃는 소리예요. 놀리거나 비웃는 느낌이 들 때도 많아요. '낄낄거리다'와 같은 뜻이고, 크고 맑게 웃는 '깔깔대다'와는 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a short, held-back laugh with the mouth mostly closed, and it often sounds like teasing or mocking. '낄낄거리다' means the same. It feels different from '깔깔대다', which is a loud, bright laugh.

examples.en: I caught a cold and couldn't go outside.
Grandmother finds it hard to go out these days.
I always wash my hands after going out.
Be careful about going outside when the fine dust is bad.
He stays at home without ever going out.
Bring a mask when you go out.

explain: 집 밖으로 나가고 들어오는 일을 말해요. '바깥출입을 삼가다', '바깥출입이 어렵다'처럼 건강, 날씨, 안전 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 평소 대화에서는 '외출'이나 '밖에 나가다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means going out of the house and coming back in. It often appears in talk of health, weather and safety, as in '바깥출입을 삼가다' (refrain from going out) and '바깥출입이 어렵다'. In ordinary conversation people more often say '외출' or '밖에 나가다'.

examples.en: My child fusses about food, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 밥투정하지 말고 한 숟가락만 먹어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't fuss about your food; just try one spoonful.

examples.ko: 밥투정이 심한 동생 때문에 엄마가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Mom has a hard time because of my little sibling's picky fussing at meals.

examples.ko: 우리 아들은 밥투정도 안 하고 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: My son eats well without any fussing about food.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 밥투정을 부리다 혼난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I got scolded for fussing over my food.

examples.ko: 밥투정 부리는 아이에게 억지로 먹이지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't force-feed a child who is fussing about food.

explain: 반찬이 마음에 안 든다고 안 먹거나 칭얼댈 때 써요. '밥투정을 부리다/하다'로 말해요. '입이 짧다'는 원래 적게 먹거나 가리는 편이라는 뜻이어서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: Used when someone refuses to eat or whines because they dislike the dishes. You say '밥투정을 부리다/하다'. '입이 짧다' means someone naturally eats little or is picky, so it differs slightly.

examples.en: The kids whisper into each other's ears.

examples.ko: 바람이 나뭇잎 사이에서 속삭거리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems like the wind is whispering among the leaves.
The students who were whispering in the library went quiet.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 속삭거리는지 자꾸 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: I keep wondering who is whispering behind me.
I whispered with my friend all night and went to bed late.
What are you two whispering about?

explain: 기본형은 '속삭이다'이고 더 많이 써요. '-거리다'가 붙으면 속삭이는 일이 계속되는 느낌이 나고, 비슷한 말로 '소곤거리다'가 있어요.
explain_en: The basic form is '속삭이다', which people use more. Adding '-거리다' gives the feeling that the whispering keeps going, and '소곤거리다' is a similar word.

examples.en: A friend saw me from far away and waved me over.
The baby gestures with a hand to call mom.
He motioned with his hand and told us to be quiet.
A police officer was signaling with his hand for the car to stop.

examples.ko: 말이 안 통해서 손짓해서 길을 물었어요.
examples.en: We couldn't understand each other, so I asked for directions with gestures.

examples.ko: 저쪽으로 가라고 손짓할 때 방향이 헷갈렸어요.
examples.en: When he gestured for me to go that way, the direction was confusing.

explain: 손짓하다는 말 없이 손으로 뜻을 전할 때 써요. '몸짓'은 몸 전체, 손짓은 손만 쓰는 점이 달라요. 보통 '~라고 손짓하다'로 이어 써요.
explain_en: 손짓하다 is for conveying a meaning with the hand without speaking. A 몸짓 uses the whole body, while a 손짓 uses just the hand. It is usually connected as ~라고 손짓하다.

examples.en: The cat crept closer.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 눈치를 보며 슬금슬금 방에서 나갔어요.
examples.en: The child sneaked out of the room, watching his mom's face.
I quietly got up before class ended.
My friend quietly took my snack.
I edged away from the gathering.
The puppy backed away bit by bit.

explain: '살금살금'은 소리 안 나게 조심하는 느낌이 강하고, 슬금슬금은 남이 모르게 슬쩍 움직이는 느낌이 강해요. 눈치를 보며 몰래 피하거나 다가갈 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '살금살금' stresses moving carefully without making a sound, while 슬금슬금 stresses moving slyly so others don't notice. It fits well when someone edges away or approaches while watching people's reactions.

examples.ko: 아이가 입을 씰룩씰룩 움직이며 울음을 참았어요.
examples.en: The child held back tears, twitching his mouth.
The rabbit whose nose keeps twitching is cute.
My shoulders shake as I hold back laughter.
His eyebrow twitched over and over.
She walks away wiggling her bottom.

examples.ko: 입꼬리가 씰룩씰룩 올라가는 걸 숨기지 못했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't hide my mouth corners twitching upward.

explain: 몸의 한 부분이 작게 반복해서 움직이는 모양을 나타내요. 보통 '씰룩거리다'와 같이 입, 코, 눈썹, 어깨 같은 말과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It shows a body part moving in small, repeated jerks. Like '씰룩거리다', it usually goes with words such as mouth, nose, eyebrow or shoulders.

examples.en: The new employee's stumbling adjustment story is really funny.

examples.ko: 처음 해외에서 산 일 년은 좌충우돌의 연속이었어요.
examples.en: My first year living abroad was one stumble after another.

examples.ko: 아이를 키우다 보면 좌충우돌하는 날이 많아요.
examples.en: When you raise a child, there are many days of bumbling along.
That movie is about young people who bumbled their way through.

examples.ko: 요리를 처음 배울 때는 누구나 좌충우돌해요.
examples.en: Everyone stumbles around when they first learn to cook.

examples.ko: 좌충우돌 끝에 드디어 첫 가게를 열었어요.
examples.en: After a lot of trial and error, I finally opened my first shop.

explain: 실수하고 부딪치면서 이리저리 헤매는 모습을 말해요. '시행착오'보다 가볍고, 조금 웃으면서 이야기하는 느낌이 있어요. '좌충우돌 성장기', '좌충우돌 적응기'처럼 제목에도 자주 붙여요.
explain_en: It describes someone making mistakes and bumping around while finding their way. It is lighter than '시행착오' and has a slightly humorous tone. It is often attached to titles, such as '좌충우돌 성장기' or '좌충우돌 적응기'.

examples.en: My younger sibling keeps mumbling something in their sleep.
He walked away, mumbling something to himself.
I memorized the words by muttering them before the exam.
I can't hear at all what you're mumbling.

examples.ko: 화가 난 아빠가 낮은 목소리로 중얼댔어요.
examples.en: My angry dad muttered in a low voice.

examples.ko: 혼자 중얼대지 말고 크게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't mumble to yourself; please say it out loud.

explain: 작고 낮은 목소리로 남이 알아듣기 어렵게 말하는 모습이에요. '중얼거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 말할 때는 '중얼거리다'를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요. 혼잣말이나 불평하는 느낌이 자주 있어요.
explain_en: It describes talking in a low, quiet voice that is hard for others to catch. It means nearly the same as '중얼거리다', which you will hear more often in speech. It often suggests talking to oneself or grumbling.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 말로 치고받다가 결국 화해했어요.
examples.en: The two traded harsh words, but in the end they made up.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 형이랑 자주 치고받고 싸웠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I often fought back and forth with my older brother.
The kids are playing around, roughhousing with each other.

examples.ko: 회의에서 두 팀이 서로 치고받는 분위기였어요.
examples.en: At the meeting, the two teams were arguing fiercely with each other.
On the debate show, the candidates traded sharp words.
The siblings were going at each other from the morning, so Mom stopped them.

explain: 서로 주고받는 상황에 써요. 몸으로 싸울 때뿐 아니라 '말로 치고받다'처럼 말다툼이 심할 때도 써요. 보통 '치고받고 싸우다'라는 형태로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when both sides give and take. It covers physical scuffles and also heated arguments, as in '말로 치고받다'. It often appears in the form '치고받고 싸우다'.

examples.en: The proposal I submitted was rejected by my team leader.
Mother rejected the clothes, saying they were too big.

examples.ko: 그 사람한테 데이트 신청했다가 퇴짜 맞았어요.
examples.en: I asked him out and got turned down.
I'm upset because I was turned down three times.

examples.ko: 가게 주인이 불량품이라며 물건에 퇴짜를 놨어요.
examples.en: The shop owner rejected the goods, saying they were defective.
What should I do if it gets rejected again?

explain: 제안, 물건, 고백 같은 것을 받아 주지 않고 거절하는 일이에요. 거절하는 쪽은 '퇴짜를 놓다', 거절당하는 쪽은 '퇴짜를 맞다'(또는 '퇴짜 당하다')라고 해요. 조금 구어체이고, 딱딱한 말로는 '거절', '반려'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is rejecting a proposal, item or confession instead of accepting it. The one who rejects says '퇴짜를 놓다', and the one rejected says '퇴짜를 맞다'. It is somewhat colloquial, and more formal words are '거절' and '반려'.

en: one step; a single step; one stride

examples.en: When I heard the news of passing, I ran over right away.
You only need to go one more step to reach the goal.

examples.ko: 한걸음 물러서서 상황을 보면 답이 보여요.
examples.en: If you step back and look at the situation, the answer shows up.
The baby took one step and then fell right down.
If you climb slowly, one step at a time, it isn't hard.
I stepped back one step in front of the door.

explain: 발을 한 번 떼어 옮기는 거리나 동작이에요. '한걸음에 달려가다'처럼 쓰면 '곧바로 서둘러'라는 뜻이고, '한걸음 물러서다'는 한발 떨어져서 본다는 뜻으로도 써요. 보통은 '한 걸음'으로 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: to run over in one stride
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번도 쉬지 않고 곧바로 급히 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to go right away in a hurry without stopping.

explain_en: It is the distance or motion of moving one foot forward once. '한걸음에 달려가다' means to rush over right away, and '한걸음 물러서다' can also mean stepping back to look at things calmly. It is also often written with a space as '한 걸음'.

en: to glare; to stare; to glower

examples.en: My younger sibling was angry and shot me a sideways glare.
Don't glare at me; say it with words.

examples.ko: 그는 옆자리 사람을 흘겨보며 한숨을 쉬었어요.
examples.en: He sighed while glaring at the person next to him.
Mom shot me a sideways glare, so I closed my mouth.

examples.ko: 사람들이 늦게 온 저를 흘겨보는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: It felt like people were glaring at me for coming late.

examples.ko: 친구가 장난으로 저를 흘겨보면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: When my friend playfully glares at me, I laugh.

explain: 못마땅하거나 밉거나 화가 나서 눈동자를 옆으로 돌려 쳐다볼 때 써요. 그냥 '쳐다보다'와 달리 감정이 담겨 있고, '눈을 흘기다'도 비슷하게 말해요. 슬쩍 한 번 보는 '흘끗 보다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when you look at someone sideways out of displeasure, dislike or anger. Unlike plain '쳐다보다', it carries emotion, and '눈을 흘기다' is a similar expression. It differs from '흘끗 보다', which means a quick glance.
